newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil groups join to partake in power firm sales.
newsitem.headline: Brazil groups join to partake in power firm sales.

text.p: Three of Brazil's largest private business groups have joined to create a holding company to bid in the privatization auctions of state-owned power firms, the groups said in a statement.

Cement and paper-pulp maker Votorantim, largest Brazilian bank Bradesco and construction giant Camargo Correa S.A. said they formed VBC Energia to seek investment opportunities in the electrical power sector.
The groups have a combined net worth of 16 billion reais, the statement said.
A panel made up of representatives of each group is being formed to draft by-laws for VBC Energia in the next 120 days, it said.

But a Memorandum of Understanding has been signed forming the holding, giving each partner an equal stockholding and rotating the chairmanship of its six-member board among them every two years, it added.
"Even before it was constituted, VBC Energia was already studying participation in privatizations foreseen for the coming months," the statement said.
The new holding may form subsidiaries with "strategic partners" and investors from Brazil and abroad to get into the business of producing and distributing electrical energy, it said.
Votorantim, Brazil's largest cement maker, owns an electrical utility firm serving 115,000 customers in Sao Paulo and Parana states, it said.
Camargo Correa, through its construction subsidiary, has participated in the construction of nine Brazilian hydroelectric projects and one hydro-plant in Venezuela, it added.
